title: Pakistan: History, Political Firsts & Amendments
desc: Firsts, leaders, treaties, wars and constitutional milestones

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
questions.e: Liaquat Ali Khan served from August 1947 until his assassination at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951. The park was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

questions.q: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
questions.e: Iskander Mirza became the first President under the 1956 Constitution; before that the head of state was the Governor-General.

questions.q: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
questions.e: Jinnah took the oath on 14-15 August 1947 and also was the first President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: Who was the first Finance Minister of Pakistan?
questions.e: Ghulam Muhammad later became Governor-General (1951-55). Ch. Muhammad Ali was Secretary-General and later PM.

questions.q: Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
questions.e: Zafarullah Khan represented Pakistan at the UN and later became a judge at the ICJ.

questions.q: Who was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
questions.e: Ayub Khan took over in January 1951, succeeding the British General Douglas Gracey.

questions.q: Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
questions.e: The SBP began operations on 1 July 1948; Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated it on that date.

questions.q: Who was the first Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan?
questions.e: The Senate was formed under the 1973 Constitution. Habibullah Khan was its first Chairman.

questions.q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
questions.e: She served 2008-2013.

questions.q: The Objectives Resolution was passed on:
questions.e: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan. It later became a substantive part of the Constitution via Article 2A.

questions.q: The first Martial Law in Pakistan was imposed on:
questions.e: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution; Ayub Khan became Chief Martial Law Administrator and removed Mirza within 20 days.

questions.q: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed Martial Law on:
questions.e: It was called Operation Fair Play and ousted Z.A. Bhutto.

questions.q: General Pervez Musharraf took power on:
questions.e: He ousted Nawaz Sharif's government after the Kargil conflict.

questions.q: The first general election in Pakistan on the basis of adult franchise was held in:
questions.e: The Awami League won 160 of 162 seats in East Pakistan; the PPP won 81 in West Pakistan.

questions.q: Which party won an absolute majority in the 1970 elections?
questions.e: Despite its majority, power was not transferred, which led to the 1971 crisis.

questions.q: The 1971 war ended on:
questions.e: Dhaka fell on 16 December. The Hamoodur Rahman Commission inquired into the debacle.

questions.q: The Agartala Conspiracy Case (1968) was linked to:
questions.e: The case alleged a conspiracy with India to separate East Pakistan. It was withdrawn in 1969.

questions.q: The Six Points of Sheikh Mujib were presented in:
questions.e: They demanded provincial autonomy and were presented at a conference of opposition parties in Lahore.

questions.q: The Tashkent Declaration was signed in:
questions.e: It ended the 1965 war and was mediated by the Soviet Union.

questions.q: The Lahore Declaration was signed by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee in:
questions.e: It was followed by the Kargil conflict in May-July 1999.

questions.q: The Kargil conflict took place in:
questions.e: It was fought in the Kargil sector of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.q: The Pakistan National Alliance (PNA) launched a movement in 1977 against the government of:
questions.e: The PNA alleged rigging in the March 1977 elections.

questions.q: Z.A. Bhutto was hanged on:
questions.e: He was convicted in a murder case; his book 'If I Am Assassinated' was written in jail.

questions.q: The Eighth Amendment (1985) is known for giving the President power to:
questions.e: It was removed by the 13th Amendment (1997), restored by the 17th (2003) and finally removed by the 18th (2010).

questions.q: The Legal Framework Order (LFO) was issued in:
questions.e: It was issued by Musharraf before the October 2002 elections and was later validated by the 17th Amendment.

questions.q: The 17th Amendment (2003) restored the President's power to:
questions.e: It was passed under the Musharraf government and removed in 2010.

questions.q: The 18th Amendment was passed in:
questions.e: It was passed under PM Yousaf Raza Gilani and President Asif Ali Zardari. It renamed NWFP to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and abolished the Concurrent List.

questions.q: Baghdad Pact, which Pakistan joined, was signed in:
questions.e: It was later renamed CENTO. Pakistan joined SEATO in 1954.

questions.q: Pakistan became a member of SEATO in:
questions.e: SEATO (South-East Asia Treaty Organization) was created in Manila in 1954.

questions.q: Pakistan left the Commonwealth in 1972 and rejoined in:
questions.e: Its membership was suspended in 1999 and 2007 due to military takeovers.

questions.q: Pakistan became a republic on:
questions.e: The Dominion status ended with the enforcement of the 1956 Constitution.

questions.q: Islamabad was selected as the capital in:
questions.e: Karachi was first capital; Rawalpindi served as interim capital. The Greek planner C.A. Doxiadis designed Islamabad.

questions.q: The Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission was set up in:
questions.e: The first nuclear power plant, KANUPP in Karachi, started in 1972.

questions.q: Pakistan's first satellite Badr-1 was launched in:
questions.e: It was launched from China. PakSat-1R and later satellites followed.

questions.q: Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in:
questions.e: He shared the prize for electroweak unification and was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate.

questions.q: The first Muslim woman Prime Minister in the world was:
questions.e: She became PM of Pakistan in December 1988 at the age of 35.

questions.q: Benazir Bhutto was assassinated on:
questions.e: She was killed after a rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi.

questions.q: The Lawyers' Movement began in March 2007 after the suspension of:
questions.e: The movement led to his restoration in 2009.

questions.q: The word 'Pakistan' was coined by:
questions.e: It appeared in the pamphlet 'Now or Never' (1933), published at Cambridge.

questions.q: The Cripps Mission came to India in:
questions.e: It offered Dominion status after WWII but was rejected by both Congress and League.

questions.q: The Simla Conference was held in:
questions.e: Viceroy Wavell convened it; it failed because of the dispute over Muslim representation.

questions.q: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in:
questions.e: Its Plan envisaged a loose federation but was not implemented.

questions.q: Direct Action Day was observed by the Muslim League on:
questions.e: It was followed by riots in Calcutta.

questions.q: The last Viceroy of British India was:
questions.e: Mountbatten announced the Partition plan on 3 June 1947.

questions.q: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in:
questions.e: It received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947.

questions.q: Liaquat Ali Khan presented the so-called 'Poor Man's Budget' in 1947 as:
o: Finance Minister in the Interim Government
questions.e: It taxed the wealthy industrialists, mostly Hindus, and angered Congress.

questions.q: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan met at Karachi on:
questions.e: Jinnah was elected its President. The famous speech of 11 August 1947 was delivered there.

questions.q: The first Constitution of Pakistan was drafted by the:
o: Second Constituent Assembly under Chaudhry Muhammad Ali
questions.e: The 1956 Constitution gave parity between East and West Pakistan and introduced One Unit.

questions.q: The One Unit scheme of West Pakistan was announced in:
questions.e: It merged the provinces of West Pakistan into one unit, which was dissolved by Yahya Khan in 1970.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced which feature in the provinces?
questions.e: It set up provincial autonomy and the 1937 elections.
